reviews.text: This is the best kind of low fantasy — the kind where the impossible is not an event but a condition, something you live alongside the way you live alongside a bad knee or a difficult neighbor. The prose is meticulous without being fussy, and the accumulation of specific detail (the Pilot G-2 07 pen, the teacher supply store that became a vape shop, the retractable metal tape measure) builds a world that feels inhabited rather than described. I particularly admire the restraint of the ending. Another story would have Linnea walk Gil into the hidden room. This one has her stand at a window listening to traffic, and the traffic is too loud, and that loudness is loss. The twenty-two notebooks are a devastating image — not because they suggest horror, but because they suggest repetition. Someone will be the twenty-fourth.
